raw_response:
I'm 57 this year, been farming these 14 mu down in Quzhou for 25 years since my father handed me the hoe. Got my middle school certificate, so I can read the extension leaflets the county sends round, but if I'm honest I trust what I see in my own fields more than what some young technician fresh from Baoding tells me. My son does construction in Shijiazhuang and my daughter-in-law sews at the garment factory, so it's mostly me and my wife on the land now. They send money home though, which means I don't have to skip fertilizer just to buy medicine.

I spread my risk — can't afford to put all my eggs in one basket on 14 mu. Five mu goes to stevia, that's our main cash crop since the buyer set up in the village five years back. Five mu for cotton, and the remaining four mu I do wheat-maize double cropping. The wheat went in last October, so right now in late March I'm looking at jointing stage. I put down base fertilizer at planting — about 15 kg of compound per mu. Now I'll topdress with urea, about 8 kg per mu. The extension sheet says 10 kg, but urea is running 2.5 yuan per jin this spring and I did 8 last year and still got 420 kg/mu. Why push my luck when cash is tight? I'll irrigate now at jointing, and once more at grain filling if the heavens stay shut. Three times total for the wheat, counting the winter irrigation I already gave it.

Come early June, that same four mu comes off the wheat and the maize goes in almost the next day — sometimes less than a week between them. I buy hybrid seed, about 55 yuan per mu. No time for plowing, I plant straight into the wheat stubble. Base fertilizer goes down at planting, about 15 kg N per mu. If the leaves yellow at jointing I'll throw another 5 kg on, but last year I didn't need to. Two irrigations for maize, and I expect around 480 kg/mu if the summer storms don't fail me.

Cotton goes in late April on the five mu south plot. I plow that field proper in early April and level it fine. Cotton's hungry — 16 kg N per mu, half at planting and half at flowering in July. The real drain is pesticides. Bollworm, aphids, weeds — I'll spray four or five times easy. Irrigate twice, at flowering and boll stage. Picking kills us, me and my wife can't bend like we used to, so I hire two women from the east village for about 15 days in September and October. Pay them 80 yuan a day, cash on the day. Hoping for 250 kg/mu of lint if the weather holds.

Stevia takes the other five mu. I plant cuttings in mid-May once the soil warms proper. Ridged the field last autumn. Stevia loves water, so three irrigations — at planting, mid-summer, and after the first cut. Lighter on fertilizer than cotton, about 12 kg N total, split between planting and after the August cut. I cut once, maybe twice if the growth is strong. Dried down I got about 240 kg/mu last year, hoping for 250 this time. The buyer pays 8 yuan per kg dry, so it's decent money, but if he drops the price like he did in 2021 I'll be cursing myself for planting so much.

All told, I'm looking at about 4,700 yuan in cash outlay this season. My son sends home 2,000 a month which takes the pressure off, but I'm still watching every coin. I thought about pushing more fertilizer on the stevia to chase a bigger yield, but a bad year with low prices would hurt more than a good year helps. Better to sleep soundly.
